findings.detail: The named l1/sources directory contains only three text extracts, not fetch receipts or original responses. The S287 quote and newline locator 241 are correct, but its claimed 5409054 PDF bytes, 531abe11d23f2e37 SHA prefix and historical fetch date cannot be re-derived from the 15284-byte text extract. S288 has the same provenance gap. S286 is independently corroborated by the committed wave-1 arxiv.html (44019 bytes and exact SHA). This is an unverifiable-original-metadata gap, not evidence that the fetch or quotation was fabricated.
findings.recommendation: Preserve original S287/S288 responses plus dated fetch-command receipts, or qualify line 32 and mark historical byte/hash/date metadata as asserted rather than independently recoverable.

gate_rechecks.result: Quote confirmed in committed abstract; committed wave-1 original HTML recomputes 44019 bytes and SHA256 7af7e470fca3ef38e97d858b308dca20e815a4b919c9c235adae4d4f59c4a86e. Historical date corroborated only by dated peer receipt, not cryptographically proven.
Exact quote confirmed at newline-delimited line 241; precision-hazard wording at line 239. Original PDF bytes/hash/date not independently recoverable from committed extract.

commands.output: Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently been used to generate mutants in both research work and in industrial practice. However, there has been no comprehensive empirical study of their performance for this increasingly important LLM-based Software Engineering application. To address this, we conduct a comprehensive empirical study evaluating BugFarm and LLMorpheus (the two state-of-the-art LLM-based approaches), alongside seven LLMs using our newly designed prompt, including both leading open- and closed-source models, on 851 real bugs from two Java real-world bug benchmarks. Our results reveal that, compared to existing rule-based approaches, LLMs generate more diverse mutants, that are behaviorally closer to real bugs and, most importantly, with 111.29% higher fault detection. That is, 87.98% (for LLMs) vs. 41.64% (for rule-based); an increase of 46.34 percentage points. Nevertheless, our results also reveal that these impressive results for improved effectiveness come at a cost: the LLM-generated mutants have worse non-compilability, duplication, and equivalent mutant rates by 26.60, 10.14, and 3.51 percentage points, respectively. These findings are immediately actionable for both research and practice. They allow practitioners to have greater confidence in deploying LLM-based mutation, while researchers now have a baseline for the state-of-the-art, with which they can research techniques to further improve effectiveness and reduce cost.

 变异测试在软件测试中的发展
• 变异测试自 1971 年被 DeMillo 和 Hamlet 提出以来，是软件测试中的重要方法
• 修改位置：从一阶变异(first order)到高阶(higher-order)，支持修改多处
• 在单元测试中：
• 面向高级语言源码：C、Java、Python、JS…
• 面向中间表示：Java bytecode, LLVM-IR
• 从桌面应用到 Android、MPI、智能合约程序等

• 从单元测试扩展到其他测试阶段：
• 集成测试
• 设计阶段（例如在基于模型的软件开发过程中针对设计FSM的变异）

 从变异测试到变异分析
• 基于变异的缺陷自动定位（mutation-based fault localization）是变异测试的衍生技术
• 缺陷自动定位：给定测试集（至少有一个未通过测试）和程序，返回程序中的语句出错可
疑度分数。
• 传统定位方法：基于测试覆盖信息对语句排序（spectrum-based fault localization）
• 基于变异的方法：通过观察变异对测试结果的改变计算可疑度
• 若一个变异使失败测试通过了，那更可能是变异了出错语句

 PART 02

痛点

 挑战1：生成高质量的变异
• 现有方法生成变异主要有两类
• 基于规则的传统方法
• PIT、Major、JavaLanche、AccMut
• 生成变异过于简单，不考虑代码上下文，文本上与真实bug差别很大

• 基于学习的方法
• 训练模型，学习真实 Bug 的代码变换模式
• DeepMutation [ICSME-19]、LEAM [ASE-22]
• 训练数据集有限，生成大量错误变异

 挑战2：可扩展性较低
• 阻碍变异分析走向工业实践的是可扩展性（Scalability）较低
• 假如有 M 个变异，N 个测试
• 变异分析的计算复杂度：O(M) + O(M×N)
• 𝑇!"!#$ = ∑%∈' 𝑡())*,% + ∑%∈' 𝑡,"%-.$),% + ∑%∈' ∑/∈0 𝑡!)(!,%,/

• 在实际规模的程序中，M 会很大

 挑战2：可扩展性较低
• 以变异测试为例，如下一行源码产生二十多个变异

 挑战3：等价变异体
• 等价变异体：变异后的程序与原始程序在功能上完全相同，即它
们对所有可能的输入产生相同的输出。
• 等价变异的危害：
• 增加测试成本

for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)
for (int i = 0; i != 10; i++)

• 影响变异分数计算的精确度

• 判断等价变异体是不可判定问题：不存在一个自动算法完美解决

 PART 03

解决思路

 面向挑战1：大模型时代的变异生成
• 大模型在代码理解和代码变换上出色的能力，为提升变异分析提
供了新的方向
• 大模型在程序修复上取得了显著的效果
• buggy -> correct

• 问题：大模型在变异分析上能否取得良好效果？

 面向挑战2：基于共享计算的加速
• 变异分析执行过程中需要反复执行测试
• 其中存在大量冗余计算
• 我们可以尝试共享冗余计算进行加速

• 大模型能否生成更接近真实bug的变异？
• 有效性：
• 语法正确

• 自然性：
• 符合一般的编程规范

• 变异足够多样，且有足够数量的变异被杀死

• 生成的有足够比例的变异能被测试检测
• 语义尽可能丰富

 PART 05

总结和展望

 基于大模型的变异生成
• 大模型在生成变异上有独特的优势
• 最大的优势在于生成行为上接近真实bug的变异
• 目前仍有很大提升空间
• 使用prompt-engineering
• 使用LLM微调
• 探索多智能体在变异生成的应用

 面向大模型的复杂变异加速
• 虽然相比于当前最新方法（SSE），已经累计加速 50x
• 当前的加速方法有一定局限性
• 仅能优化限定代码区间的简单变异

# LLM-era mutants raise fault detection and raise equivalence at the same time, and equivalence is declared undecidable

Admitted in round 58 from the shokuknow `corpus-expansion-1` package
(`merge/tameshi/knowledge/corpus/knowledge/llm-mutant-equivalence-cost.md`, staged ids S156/S165,
re-pointed by document to S286/S287 after the id-collision check; package text adapted before
landing — this entry is the lane's own re-grounding, not a byte copy).

## What the sources state

- S286 evaluates LLM-generated mutants against rule-based ones on 851 real
  bugs from two Java bug benchmarks: the LLM mutants are "more diverse ...
  behaviorally closer to real bugs and, most importantly, with 111.29% higher
  fault detection", but "the LLM-generated mutants have worse non-compilability,
  duplication, and equivalent mutant rates by 26.60, 10.14, and 3.51 percentage
  points, respectively" (§Abstract, verified present in the copy opened 2026-10-30).
- S287 states the equivalence class — "等价变异体：变异后的程序与原始程序在功能上完全相同" — and records
  the hazards of that class: it "影响变异分数计算的精确度" (degrades the precision of the
  mutation score), and deciding equivalence is undecidable in general:
  "判断等价变异体是不可判定问题：不存在一个自动算法完美解决" (extract lines 230-241; the class
  definition itself is line 231).

## What this means for the lane's survivor classes

- **A survivor is not yet a test hole.** The lane's survivor classes (its
  own arm-class matrix, and the B5 / D2 / D10 survivors) are all cases where
  a mutant was *not killed*. S286 shows that in an LLM-mutant setting a
  materially larger share of un-killed mutants are equivalent. Inference: an
  LLM-era survivor must be classified against an equivalence witness before
  it is counted as a gap in the suite — the same non-equivalence witness the
  lane already requires for rule-based mutants.
- **Three counters, not one.** S286 reports non-compilability, duplication
  and equivalence as three separate rates. The lane's F1 note (compile and
  runtime errors excluded from the score, per its held S001) means a
  non-compilating LLM mutant must not silently enter the denominator.
  Inference: an LLM-era sweep needs three counters.
- **The two literatures agree on the hazard.** S286 quantifies the
  equivalence rate in English; S287 states the same hazard in Chinese and
  adds an explicit statement that the problem admits no automatic solution.

## Boundary of this entry

- S286 is measured on Java and on real-world bug benchmarks; the lane's legs
  are one JavaScript gate and one bash gate. The transfer is **not
  measured**: no lane sweep has produced an LLM-generated mutant yet, and
  the entry supplies the counting contract, not a measurement.
- Equivalence stays undecidable (S287): a witness is per-mutant evidence
  (an input where the mutant and the original differ), never a general
  decision procedure. The lane's 1-minimality witness
  (`corpus/knowledge/delta-debugging-minimization-contract.md`) reduces a
  failing case; it does not decide equivalence.
- The F9 pilot move (a bounded LLM-mutant pilot with an independent outcome
  check) remains unmeasured; this entry does not close it.
